content:
The test image shows open soybean pods with visible white/gray cottony growth inside, dark/blackened seeds, and brown pod walls. Key features: white fluffy material inside pod, severely discolored/dark seeds.

Top candidates: **White_Mold** (white cottony seeds in pods, black sclerotia), **Phomopsis** (gray mold on cracked/shriveled seeds).

The White Mold reference shows white fluffy cottony growth with black sclerotia on pods/stems. Phomopsis shows circular pycnidia rings on pod surfaces. The test image clearly shows white/gray cottony mycelial growth inside the pod cavity surrounding dark-colored seeds — this matches White Mold's hallmark "white cottony seeds in pods" description.

**Analysis:**

The test image shows:
- Open/split dry brown soybean pod
- White-gray cottony/fluffy mycelial growth inside the pod cavity
- Seeds heavily darkened/discolored, coated with white-gray mold
- Pod walls with brown lesions and dark spots

The White Mold reference confirms the same white fluffy cottony growth pattern with black sclerotia embedded in the mold on stems and pods. The test image represents an advanced stage where the pod has opened, revealing the characteristic "white cottony seeds in pods" — the definitive diagnostic feature of White Mold (Sclerotinia stem rot).

Phomopsis was eliminated: its reference shows distinctive circular pycnidia ring lesions on pod surface, not white internal cottony growth.
